mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate relative to its 12-month moving average signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns in periods where FEDFUNDS is declining (relative to 12-month MA) are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 4.0%, it signals a weakening labor market that prompts central bank intervention and increased fiscal stimulus, which historically has led to a rebound in equity prices over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: In instances where UNRATE > 4.0%, the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of cases, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and industrial production (INDPRO) indicates robust economic activity across both consumer and business sectors, which typically precedes stronger corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising HOUST and INDPRO fails to predict positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of cases, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During post-crisis recovery periods, a decline in the federal funds rate below 4.5% signals the central bank's commitment to supporting economic growth, which drives S&P 500 forward returns positively over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In the post-crisis recovery regime, the 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) relative to its 12-month moving average indicates a strengthening labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns in periods of rising PAYEMS (relative to 12-month MA) are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate rises above 5.0%, it signals a tightening monetary policy that increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate investment, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: In instances where FEDFUNDS > 5.0%, the 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of cases, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle expansion, a decline in consumer credit outstanding (RSAFS) relative to its 12-month moving average signals a potential slowdown in consumer spending, which typically precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In the late-cycle expansion regime, the 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a strong economy with tight labor market and monetary policy, which historically has led to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to inflation concerns.
regime_hint: tight labor market with monetary tightening
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising FEDFUNDS and falling UNRATE fails to predict negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of cases, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.
